9	# Smoothness of the Jacobian (W5-S2), and the shape of the relative-dimension assembly
10	
11	Brick S2 of the Wave-5 abelian-variety package (roadmap `AJCR.w5-av.s2`):
12	`Smooth d.J.hom` for the pinned representability datum `(d : JacobianData C)`,
13	via mathlib's group-scheme smoothness criterion.
14	
15	## Why this is one line, and what it costs
16	
17	`smooth_of_grpObj` (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Smooth.lean:64`) needs three
18	hypotheses on `f`, and the datum supplies two of them outright:
19	
20	* `[LocallyOfFiniteType f]` — `d.locallyOfFiniteType`, a construction certificate;
21	* `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` — `d.grpObj`. Note the **keying**: instance search does
22	  not unfold `Over.mk` on its own, so the group structure must be ascribed at the
23	  `Over.mk d.J.hom` spelling. This is pure defeq (`Over.mk d.J.hom` *is* `d.J` by
24	  structure eta) and `Picard/JacobianData.lean` machine-checks exactly this as its
25	  η-defeq smoke test 2;
26	* `[GeometricallyReduced f]` — brick **S1**, which is *not* proved here. It stays
27	  an instance argument, so this file is unconditional in the datum and every
28	  consumer sees the S1 dependency in its own signature.
29	
30	Geometric (rather than bare) reducedness is intrinsic to mathlib's route, not an
31	artefact: the proof base-changes to `AlgebraicClosure k`, runs the homogeneity
32	argument there — translating the smooth locus by `GrpObj.mulRight` until it meets
33	any prescribed closed point — and descends along
34	`@Surjective ⊓ @Flat ⊓ @QuasiCompact`. That is also why S1 is naturally stated
35	geometrically; see `informal/w5-s-worksheet.md` §1–§2.
36	
37	## Main declarations
38	
39	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.smooth` — `Smooth d.J.hom`, given S1.
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.smooth_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension` — the
41	  degradation direction of the frozen numeral, recorded so that S3's consumers
42	  need not re-derive `Smooth` from `SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C)`.
43	
44	The S3 assembly itself (`SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) d.J.hom`) is
45	**worksheet-first** and its route is frozen in `informal/w5-s-worksheet.md` §3;
46	the short version is that mathlib's `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` is a *pointwise,
47	local-at-source* condition, so no "relative dimension is locally constant"
48	theorem is needed — translation homogeneity (X2) transports the identity count
49	(T5) to the other points. No Lean is written for S3 here: its numeral waits on
50	T3/T4.
51	
52	Reference: Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §5 `cor:sm` (arXiv:math/0504020);
53	Milne, "Abelian varieties", Prop. 2.1.
54	-/

67	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
68	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
69	
70	/-- **S2: the Jacobian is smooth over `k`** (Kleiman §5 `cor:sm`). A group scheme
71	locally of finite type and geometrically reduced over a field is smooth
72	(`smooth_of_grpObj`); the first two hypotheses come from the datum, and geometric
73	reducedness is brick S1, taken here as an instance argument. -/
74	theorem smooth (d : JacobianData C) [GeometricallyReduced d.J.hom] : Smooth d.J.hom :=
75	  letI := d.locallyOfFiniteType
76	  letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
77	  smooth_of_grpObj d.J.hom
78	
79	/-- The frozen numeral degrades to bare smoothness: if the Jacobian is smooth of
80	relative dimension `genus C` (brick S3) then it is smooth. Recorded here so
81	consumers of the S3 instance need not rediscover
82	`SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth`, and so that the two statements of the
83	smoothness leg sit side by side. -/
84	theorem smooth_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension (d : JacobianData C)
85	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) d.J.hom] : Smooth d.J.hom :=
86	  SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth (n := genus C) d.J.hom
87	
88	end JacobianData
89	
90	end AlgebraicGeometry

55	## §2 S1 — `GeometricallyReduced d.J.hom` (WORKSHEET-FIRST, risk R2)
56	
57	Route **α1** confirmed as the only live candidate; α2 (dimension count) remains unstateable
58	(mathlib has no scheme dimension theory — re-verified). But the recon's α1 sketch conflates
59	two steps of quite different cost, and naming that split is this section's job.
60	
61	α1 as the recon states it: square-zero lifts of `k̄`-points of the *functor* all exist
62	because the obstruction is an `H²` of a two-term complex, identically zero ⟹ `𝒪_{J_k̄,0}`
63	formally smooth ⟹ regular ⟹ reduced at `0` ⟹ (spread by translations, X2) `IsReduced J_k̄`
64	⟹ geometrically reduced.
65	
66	**The two-term-`H²`=0 half is the cheap half, and it is cheap for a structural reason.**
67	`pic0Functor` is defined through `picEt`, whose values are Čech classes on a **two**-chart
68	affine cover (`Tangent/TruncExpCech.lean`, brick T2, landed). A two-term Čech complex has no
69	degree-2 term *at all*: the obstruction group is not "computed to be zero", it is absent by
70	construction. This is the curve-lite replacement the recon wanted for Kleiman `prp:H2`, and
71	it is why the standing instruction never to port EGA III 7.7.5/7.7.10 Exchange (descope
72	boundary R6, `w5-recon.md` §1.4) costs nothing here.
73	
74	**The expensive half is the ring-level bridge**, and the recon flags it correctly but
75	understates it: *"functor-lifts ⇒ local ring formally smooth ⇒ regular/reduced"*. Probing the
76	three links:
77	
78	| link | status in pinned mathlib |
79	|---|---|
80	| square-zero lifting criterion for `FormallySmooth` | **present** — `Algebra.FormallySmooth.iff_comp_surjective` / `comp_surjective` (`RingTheory/Smooth/Basic.lean:83`) |
81	| formally smooth local `k̄`-algebra ⇒ regular | **PARTIAL** — the general statement is Cohen-structure-flavoured; what mathlib has is `RegularLocalRing` API (`RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/Defs.lean`) and smooth⇒regular for *scheme* morphisms, not the local-algebra implication under a bare `FormallySmooth` |
82	| regular local ⇒ reduced | **present** — regular local rings are domains, hence reduced |
83	| `IsReduced J_k̄` ⇒ `GeometricallyReduced` | **ABSENT — see the retraction in §2.1.** I first read `Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean` as supplying this; it supplies the converse (`Smooth ⇒ GeometricallyReduced`), which would be circular here |
84	
85	So R2's real content is link 2, and it is a **local-algebra** gap, not a geometric one.
86	
87	**RECOMMENDED REFRAME, and the reason to write this worksheet before the Lean.** Do not go
88	through `FormallySmooth` on the local ring at all. Mathlib's own group-scheme route (§1)
89	only ever needs `IsReduced` of the `k̄`-fibre, and `IsReduced` of a scheme is a *stalkwise*
90	condition. The functor-lifting input gives, at the identity, that every square-zero
91	thickening of a `k̄`-point lifts — which is exactly the statement that the local ring has no
92	nonzero nilpotent *in the direction of the cotangent space*, and the two-term complex makes
93	that direction-wise statement uniform. Concretely the brick to state is
94	
95	> **S1-a**: for the identity point `0` of `J_k̄`, the stalk `𝒪_{J_k̄,0}` is reduced,
96	
97	proved from the ε-kernel computation (T3/T4 at `K := k̄`, which route (ii) of the t4 worksheet
98	supplies *uniformly in `K`* — this is exactly the payoff the t4 worksheet promised in its
99	"why (ii) over (i)" item 3), and then
100	
101	> **S1-b**: `IsReduced J_k̄` from S1-a by translation homogeneity (X2, landed:
102	> `AbelianVariety/Translation.lean`, which already exports the exact transport
103	> `isReduced_stalk_pointTranslationIso_iff`), and then `GeometricallyReduced d.J.hom`.
104	
105	**Gate**: S1-a genuinely needs T3/T4. It cannot be started before them, and pretending
106	otherwise is how this lane burned sessions before.
107	
108	### 2.1 CORRECTION to my own §2 above: S1-b is NOT [S], and the reason is a mathlib gap
109	
110	I wrote "S1-b is startable now and is [S]" one paragraph ago on the strength of
111	`Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean` being available. **That was wrong and I am retracting it
112	in the same document** (the project's retraction discipline, I-0494). What that file
113	actually proves is the implication in the *other* direction —
114	`Smooth f ⟹ GeometricallyReduced f` (`:130`), plus
115	`SmoothOfRelativeDimension n f ⟹ GeometricallyReduced f` (`:147`). Using it for S1 would be
116	circular: S2 derives `Smooth` *from* `GeometricallyReduced`.
117	
118	What S1-b actually needs is the descent step
119	
120	> `IsReduced (J ×_k k̄)` ⟹ `GeometricallyReduced d.J.hom`,
121	
122	i.e. "reduced after base change to the algebraic closure ⟹ reduced after base change to
123	*every* field extension". Checked this session, and this is the finding:
